nodes.title: MuJoCo calculates the response.

representation-map.title: Ways to describe the same 3D cabinet
representation-map.intro: Representation is the information kept about the object.

nodes.title: Point cloud
nodes.text: 3D positions; optional colors.

nodes.title: Mesh
nodes.text: Vertices and connected triangle or quad faces.

nodes.title: CAD boundary representation
nodes.text: Mathematical curves and surfaces, their boundaries, and their connections.

nodes.title: Voxel grid
nodes.text: Values in small 3D cells, such as occupied or empty.

nodes.title: 3D Gaussians
nodes.text: Positions, sizes, orientations, opacities, and appearance.

nodes.title: Signed distance (SDF)
nodes.text: How far from the surface, and on which side?

nodes.title: Occupancy
nodes.text: Is this location inside the solid, or how likely is it to be inside?

nodes.title: Radiance field
nodes.text: Density and view-dependent color. NeRF represents a field with a neural network.

representation-map.note: Storage and field meaning can be combined. A voxel grid can store sampled distance or occupancy values.
representation-map.caption: A field describes what we can ask; its storage describes how the answers are kept. For example, a voxel grid can store an occupancy value in every cell.

nodes.text: Calculate contacts and motion over short time steps.

nodes.title: Task feedback
nodes.text: Provide the next image or state values, reward, and success information.

task-loop.intro: An action is executed; its outcome becomes the next observation.
task-loop.repeat: Return the new observation to the policy while the episode continues.
task-loop.note: End the attempt using the experiment’s stopping rule or time limit, then reset.
task-loop.caption: One policy action may span many short physics steps. The renderer creates camera images from the updated scene; task code computes the reward and success flag.
